label: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
output:
Here's your letter, all fixed up and ready to copy-paste into the group text or email. I kept your voice — warm, a little funny, and not too polished — so it sounds like you, not like a business.

---

**Subject: Lotus Glow Nails update — everybody ok, and here's where to find me 🩷**

Hi everybody,

You all ask me the same question all day, so I write one message and please pass it along to whoever need it.

Sunday night around 2am, a lady's car went straight through my salon front window on Bellaire Blvd. She was not inside, thank God. She is ok, police come, and her insurance is paying. Nobody hurt. The damage is the front glass is gone and one pedicure chair is smashed.

Right now the city inspector must check the wall before I can open the door. My contractor say we reopen Monday, November 16. I will text you all the minute that door open again.

This week, me and Trang and Kim are working at my cousin Hoa's salon, **Pearland Nail Bar**. If you need your nails this week, please go there, or call/text me at my cell **832-555-0147** and we will find you a time.

Now the good part. My floor look like a rainbow throw up. My husband look at it and say, "Finally, this shop is modern art." 😄 And that car stop exactly at the pedicure chair — like she was coming for a spa. My daughter say the driver get the first drive-thru pedicure in Houston. I cannot argue with that.

I am ok. I cry a little in the morning, but now I am fine. God protect us, because if that car had hit when somebody was sitting in that chair... Please do not worry about me.

Your gift card still good. Nobody lose nothing. When we open again, come early — we have a lot of nail to catch up on.

Thank you for all the text, the phone call, and the food. Special thank you to Mrs. Dung, who bring pho to me this morning. You people keep me going.

Love,
[Your name]
Lotus Glow Nails — 11 years on Bellaire Blvd

---

Two small things: put your name in the signature line, and send it to Mrs. Dung and the others who helped first, so they can share it too. If the group text feel too long, tell me and I'll cut a short 4-line version for the text and keep the full one for email.
